question: What should a singer do when singing is difficult or breath runs short?
answer: When singing high notes or leaping notes, if too much force is applied, it can lead to situations where you run out of breath or cannot take a proper breath in the next phrase. Gently finish high notes and make full use of the rests between notes to allow for proper breathing.

question: What should I do if the first note does not come out well when a phrase begins on a high note?
answer: It is not easy to sing a high note at the beginning of a phrase. It is common to connect the half note of the previous phrase without pausing in the middle to flexibly and clearly produce the ‘환한속에 구름처럼’ of ‘구’, which is a choice many vocalists take. If you are forced to end the previous phrase and take a breath before singing the high note of the next phrase, it is better to maintain the feeling and vocalization used in the previous phrase as much as possible to carry it over to the next phrase.
